update.answer:
The document describes two very different kinds of signals:

| Modality | What it measures | How the signal is generated |
|----------|------------------|-----------------------------|
| **MEG (Magnetoencephalography)** | Tiny magnetic fields that arise when neurons fire electrical currents. | Electrical activity in brain cells creates a magnetic field; ultra‑sensitive SQUID detectors pick up these magnetic “ripples.” |
| **MRS (Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy)** | The concentrations of specific brain chemicals (metabolites) such as neurotransmitters, energy substrates, etc. | It uses magnetic‑resonance principles to detect the resonant frequencies of different molecules, giving a chemical “profile” of the tissue. |

**In short:** MEG records the **magnetic fields** produced by neuronal electrical activity, whereas MRS records the **chemical signals** (metabolite levels) detected by magnetic‑resonance spectroscopy.
